elements.element: Customer is not subject to any restriction on soliciting the other party’s employees or personnel.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly prohibits both parties, including Customer, from directly soliciting certain employees of the other party.

elements.element: The non-solicitation obligation is mutual and applies reciprocally to both parties.
elements.evidence: The clause provides that “neither party shall” directly solicit covered employees.

elements.element: The non-solicitation restriction is limited to personnel directly involved in the services.
elements.evidence: The restriction applies only to an employee of the other party “who was directly involved in the provision of services under this Agreement.”

elements.element: For each covered individual, the non-solicitation restriction ends no later than 12 months after that individual’s involvement in the services ends.
elements.evidence: Although the clause references 12 months following the end of an individual’s involvement, it also applies independently “[d]uring the term.” If an individual’s involvement ends more than 12 months before the Agreement terminates, the restriction continues for the remainder of the term and therefore exceeds the permitted individual-specific period.

elements.element: General advertisements and other recruitment activity not specifically targeted at the other party’s personnel are excluded.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly excludes “general advertisements or other recruitment activity not specifically targeted at the other party’s personnel.”

elements.element: Unsolicited approaches initiated by an individual are excluded.
elements.evidence: The clause does not apply to “any person who approaches a party on his or her own initiative.”

elements.element: The clause does not prohibit hiring and contains no no-hire restriction.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly states that it “does not prohibit either party from hiring any person,” while restricting only direct solicitation.

result.reason: The redline rejects the preferred position because Customer remains bound by a non-solicit. It substantially implements the fallback, including mutuality, the directly involved personnel limitation, both required carve-outs, and removal of the no-hire. However, the independent “during the term” language can extend the restriction beyond 12 months after an individual’s involvement ends, so the fallback is not fully satisfied. The clause otherwise remains coherent and does not disturb unrelated commercial terms.
